referenceYear.description: Year the assessment is made; EOL distances and ages are measured from here.

functionalCoverage.description: Weight of functional coverage in business value (weights sum to 1).
functionalCoverage.rationale: Analyst judgement: coverage matters, but a system can cover its function and still be strategically irrelevant.

userSatisfaction.description: Weight of user satisfaction in business value.
userSatisfaction.rationale: Kept lowest because satisfaction scores are the noisiest input (survey-based, loud minorities).

strategicRelevance.description: Weight of strategic relevance in business value.
strategicRelevance.rationale: Rationalisation is driven by the target operating model, so fit with strategy carries most weight together with criticality.

businessCriticality.description: Weight of business criticality (1–5) in business value.
businessCriticality.rationale: Systems that stop revenue or production when down must never land in a low-value quadrant by accident.

supportability.description: Weight of supportability (skills, vendor support) in technical health (weights sum to 1).
supportability.rationale: Key-person dependency is the most common operational risk in legacy custom systems.

security.description: Weight of security posture in technical health.
security.rationale: Equal to supportability; unpatchable systems are a board-level risk (NIS2-era expectations).

scalability.description: Weight of scalability in technical health.
scalability.rationale: An industrial group with stable volumes rarely hits scale limits; kept below security and supportability.

documentation.description: Weight of documentation quality in technical health.
documentation.rationale: Matters for migration effort but is partly captured by supportability.

eolRisk.description: Weight of the EOL-risk sub-score (5 = platform far from end of life).
eolRisk.rationale: The data-center exit makes platform age a first-order driver in this case.

alreadyExpired.description: Subtracted from technical health when the platform is already past vendor end of support.
alreadyExpired.rationale: Explicit penalty per method spec, on top of the eolRisk sub-score, so an unsupported platform cannot be offset by good documentation.

expiresWithinWindow.description: Subtracted from technical health when the platform reaches end of support within the window.
expiresWithinWindow.rationale: Half of the expired penalty: still supported, but an upgrade is unavoidable within the planning horizon.

windowYears.description: Look-ahead window for the 'expires soon' penalty.
windowYears.rationale: Typical lead time for an upgrade or replacement project in an enterprise.

valueThreshold.description: Business value at or above this is 'high value'.
valueThreshold.rationale: Midpoint of the 1–5 scale; tested for a plausible quadrant split in the engine tests.

healthThreshold.description: Technical health at or above this is 'high health'.
healthThreshold.rationale: Midpoint of the 1–5 scale; tested for a plausible quadrant split in the engine tests.

nonPrimaryDuplicate.description: Category forced on non-primary members of a duplicate group (same L2 capability).
nonPrimaryDuplicate.rationale: Standard post-merger consolidation logic: keep one standard per capability, retire the rest.

eolMigrateMaxYearsToEol.description: Platforms reaching end of support in fewer than this many years trigger the 'at least Migrate' override.
eolMigrateMaxYearsToEol.rationale: Matches the eolPenalty window: less than one planning cycle left.

eolMigrateMinCriticality.description: Minimum business criticality for the EOL override.
eolMigrateMinCriticality.rationale: Only business-critical systems justify forcing action; low-criticality EOL systems follow the normal quadrant.

lowComplexityMaxIntegrations.description: A Tolerate system on-prem with at most this many integrations counts as low complexity (→ Rehost).
lowComplexityMaxIntegrations.rationale: Beyond three interfaces a lift-and-shift typically needs integration re-testing that resembles a replatform.

lowComplexitySizeClasses.description: Size classes that count as low complexity for Rehost.
lowComplexitySizeClasses.rationale: L/XL systems usually carry clustering, licensing or performance constraints that make pure rehosting risky.

refactorMinBusinessValue.description: Migrate + custom systems at or above this business value are refactored; below it they are replatformed.
refactorMinBusinessValue.rationale: Refactoring is the most expensive route; reserve it for clearly high-value custom systems.

investRefactorSizeClasses.description: Invest + on-prem systems in these size classes are refactored; smaller ones are replatformed.
investRefactorSizeClasses.rationale: Large strategic systems benefit most from cloud-native redesign; small ones get most of the value from a managed platform.

residencyFlagSensitivity.description: Systems with this sensitivity and residencyRequired are flagged 'requires EU/NO region'.
residencyFlagSensitivity.rationale: GDPR art. 9 special-category data (e.g. health) is where residency requirements are typically set by policy.

fteLoadedCostNok.description: Fully loaded internal cost of one IT FTE (salary, employer tax, pension, overhead). Used to express supportFte cost.
fteLoadedCostNok.rationale: Rough Norwegian IT-specialist salary level plus employer contributions and overhead; not from a benchmark.

infraFactor.description: Target annual infrastructure cost relative to today's infra cost, per 6R.
infraFactor.rationale: Lift-and-shift saves little until rightsized; managed services and cloud-native designs save progressively more; repurchase moves hosting into the subscription.

supportFteFactor.description: Target internal support effort relative to today, per 6R.
supportFteFactor.rationale: Less patching and OS work on managed platforms; SaaS still needs application management and vendor governance.

licenseFactor.description: Target license and vendor-support cost relative to today, per 6R (repurchase uses the subscription parameters instead).
licenseFactor.rationale: Replatforming often drops commercial DB/OS licences; refactoring removes more of them.

repurchaseSubscriptionFactor.description: Annual SaaS subscription after repurchase, relative to today's license, vendor support and infra.
repurchaseSubscriptionFactor.rationale: SaaS subscriptions bundle hosting and upgrades and commonly cost more than on-prem maintenance alone; savings come from internal effort, not licences.

repurchaseMinSubscriptionNok.description: Floor for a replacement SaaS subscription.
repurchaseMinSubscriptionNok.rationale: Avoids unrealistically cheap replacements for custom systems with near-zero licence cost today.

cloudRunCostMultiplier.description: Scales all new cloud run cost (cloud infra after rehost/replatform/refactor and SaaS subscriptions after repurchase). Dashboard slider; the sensitivity analysis varies it ±sensitivityRange.
cloudRunCostMultiplier.rationale: Neutral default; the per-6R infra factors carry the estimate. Exposed because cloud price and rightsizing discipline are the largest run-cost uncertainty.

consolidationRunCostFactor.description: Extra run cost on the primary system when a duplicate is consolidated into it (more users/licences/capacity).
consolidationRunCostFactor.rationale: Users move to the group standard rather than disappearing; enterprise agreements usually price extra seats well below a separate product, so roughly a third of the old licence spend reappears.

migrationCostNok.description: One-off migration cost per 6R and size class, before the integration-complexity multiplier.
migrationCostNok.rationale: Order-of-magnitude project sizes (weeks to years of effort at the day rate below); relative ordering rehost < replatform < repurchase < refactor follows common migration practice.

migrationCostMultiplier.description: Scales the price of all one-off costs (migration, consolidation, temporary integrations). Dashboard slider; effort in person-days and hence the roadmap are unaffected.
migrationCostMultiplier.rationale: Neutral default; models rate-card and overrun uncertainty separately from the effort estimates so the roadmap stays stable while the business case is stress-tested.

consolidationCostNok.description: Extra one-off cost when a retirement consolidates a duplicate into the primary: data migration, user onboarding and re-pointing interfaces. Added to the retire cost and scaled by the integration-complexity multiplier.
consolidationCostNok.rationale: Consolidation is a real migration project (e.g. NAV into SAP, BizTalk into Azure Integration Services), so it is costed at roughly half to two-thirds of a replatform of the same size rather than as a free switch-off.

dayRateNok.description: Blended internal/consultant day rate; converts migration cost to person-days for roadmap capacity.
dayRateNok.rationale: Blend of internal staff and Norwegian consultancy rates; not from a published rate card.

integrationComplexityPerIntegration.description: Migration cost multiplier = 1 + this × number of integrations (inbound + outbound), capped below.
integrationComplexityPerIntegration.rationale: Each interface needs re-pointing and regression testing, roughly a few person-days to weeks each.

integrationComplexityMaxMultiplier.rationale: Hub systems are migrated with interface virtualisation; cost does not scale linearly forever.

dataCenterAnnualFixedCostNok.description: Facility cost of the leased data center (lease, power, cooling, physical security) not allocated to individual systems; avoided after DC exit.
dataCenterAnnualFixedCostNok.rationale: Plausible for a mid-size enterprise data hall; fictional company, no benchmark used.

discountRate.rationale: Corporate cost-of-capital level for an industrial company; deliberately above the 4 % real rate Finansdepartementet prescribes for public projects (R-109/2021). Adjustable in the dashboard.

horizonYears.rationale: Common horizon for IT investment cases; long enough to capture payback of refactors.

sensitivityRange.description: Range applied to cloud run-cost factors and migration costs in the sensitivity analysis.
sensitivityRange.rationale: Reflects the uncertainty in unbenchmarked factors; wide enough to test whether the recommendation flips.

startQuarter.description: First quarter of the migration programme.
startQuarter.rationale: Programme mobilised after budget approval in Q4 2026.

endQuarter.description: Last quarter of the migration programme.
endQuarter.rationale: Three-year programme; post-DC-exit refactors complete in 2029.

maxSystemsPerQuarter.description: Maximum number of systems cut over in one quarter.
maxSystemsPerQuarter.rationale: Limited by change-freeze windows, business testing capacity and hypercare.

maxPersonDaysPerQuarter.rationale: Roughly 25 FTE across internal staff and partners (~60 productive days per quarter each).

dcExitMilestone.description: Hard milestone: every data-center-hosted system that is not site-bound must be retired or moved by the end of this quarter.
dcExitMilestone.rationale: Data-center lease expires in 2028 in the case narrative.

waves.description: Wave assignment by 6R: quick-win retirements first, heavy transformations last. Retain is not scheduled.
waves.rationale: Standard migration sequencing: free capacity and cost early, build cloud skills on simple moves before complex ones.

rehostWaveMaxIntegrations.description: Rehost candidates with more integrations than this move to wave 2.
rehostWaveMaxIntegrations.rationale: Wave 1 should be low-risk moves that build migration muscle.

temporaryIntegrationPersonDays.description: Effort to build a temporary bridge when a system moves before a dependency (e.g. to break a cycle).
temporaryIntegrationPersonDays.rationale: A simple hybrid connection (VPN/API proxy) plus testing; rough estimate.
